task: book or pay for parking, or buy a transit fare, online (SpotHero, ParkMobile, city meter apps, transit fare apps): find the location or enter the zone number, pick a time window or fare type, pay; complete when the parking pass, active session, or purchased fare is on screen. Surface pinned: a parking or transit website/app — not a physical pay station or meter. Variants: paying a parking ticket or fine, monthly parking contracts, and airport parking bundled with flights do not belong.

tree.note: 1 where the app or the site still has to be reached - A2Q arrives by scanning a sign and Kj30 opens straight onto the zone prompt. 2 to pick which of the several things this app sells. then 3 and 4 in either order: A2Q cannot pick a duration until a car exists, while 8GuH names both stations first and its passenger counts last. 5 bounds the purchase, and in the parking half the bound is a clock that starts on payment. 6 wherever a price is on screen, which is more than once in five keepers. 7 in every keeper that pays. 8 as soon as the artifact appears, and 8.7 when it never does. 9 afterwards; Kj30 runs 5 to 8 a second time to extend a session that is already running.

questions.why: This matters because tapping complete order finalizes the $5.00 charge, and the app requires a decision on location access to proceed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the chance to review the final total and decide whether to grant the app access to your current location.
questions.verify_form: The agent placed the order and answered a location prompt at the same moment - check both; the order is the charge and the prompt is separate from it.
questions.check: Does completing the order charge the shown amount, and does the app separately ask for location access at the same moment?
questions.say_example: This charges <$5.00> now and also asks to use your location. Ready for both, or should I hold?

children.label: Write the value to the card

questions.question: Does the screen show a top-up success message after tapping the card?
questions.why: The app explicitly prompts you to tap and hold the EZ-Link card to the phone to transfer the funds and verify the updated balance.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An AI agent cannot physically hold a smart card against the device to complete an NFC-based transaction.
questions.check: Does the screen show a top-up success message after the card is tapped against the phone?
questions.say_example: The screen never showed a top-up success message after the tap. The balance may not have moved to the card.

questions.question: Did the app block your payment attempt with an error popup?
questions.why: The user clicked the R-Wallet payment option despite the screen showing an 'Insufficient Balance' warning, causing the app to throw a hard error popup that had to be dismissed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the chance to acknowledge the payment failure and actively decide how to resolve it, such as by topping up the wallet or choosing a different method.
questions.check: Did the app show an error popup blocking the payment attempt?
questions.say_example: Payment blocked - insufficient balance error shown

questions.question: Did the payment fail and prompt you to select a different payment method?
questions.why: Transactions can be declined by the bank or gateway, requiring you to notice the error message and choose an alternative card to complete the booking.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to step in and provide a backup payment method if your primary choice is rejected.
questions.verify_form: The agent hit a declined payment and either tried a different method or stopped - check what it did; a second attempt on a different card can also mean two holds on your money.
questions.check: Did the payment get declined, and does the page prompt for a different payment method?
questions.say_example: That card was declined. I can try a different one, but a second attempt can leave two holds on your money at once.

children.label: Confirm the pass or ticket
children.note: 8.1 the moment the artifact appears. 8.2 where it is a code that has to be shown or scanned. 8.3 where what was bought is a running clock rather than a document. 8.4 where the terms of use only arrive with the artifact. 8.5 where the app's own screens disagree. 8.6 where the artifact has to be saved or found again. 8.7 when nothing is issued at all - four keepers, and in x--I something is issued for the wrong journey.

children.label: Read the issued pass or ticket

questions.question: What are the details and validity of your booked ticket?
questions.why: The screen displays the journey ticket details, including the route, passenger count, fare, and validity time.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to verify the ticket details and understand its validity conditions firsthand.
questions.check: What route, passenger count, fare, and validity does the issued ticket show?
questions.say_example: Ticket issued - <Borivali to Surat>, <2 passengers>, <₹500>, valid until <6:00 PM>

questions.question: Is the final digital ticket or active session actually displayed on the screen?
questions.why: Because the mobile display acts as the travel authority for paperless bookings, the actual ticket must be visible to confirm the transaction succeeded.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the necessary proof of payment to legally park or ride if the agent stops before the digital pass is generated and displayed.
questions.check: Does the screen actually display a final digital ticket, active session, or QR code with a validity period, distinct from merely completing the purchase steps?
questions.say_example: The steps finished, but no ticket or active session actually shows on this screen.

children.label: Check the code that gets scanned

questions.question: Does the downloaded pass show the correct QR code and acknowledgement details?
questions.why: You need to verify that the downloaded PNG clearly displays the QR code, acknowledgement number, and validity dates so you can successfully use the transit pass.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the peace of mind of personally verifying that the downloaded transit pass image contains a legible, scannable QR code before closing the file.
questions.check: Does the downloaded pass file actually show a QR code, an acknowledgement number, and validity dates?
questions.say_example: The downloaded pass doesn't actually show a QR code or acknowledgement number, even though the download said it would.

children.label: Read the rules that come with it

questions.question: What restrictions apply to this digital ticket?
questions.why: The screen lists strict conditions for the ticket, including a one-hour validity window, non-refundability, and device-locking, which are critical to know before proceeding.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to review the strict validity and device-locking rules, potentially leaving them with an unusable or expired ticket if they aren't ready to travel immediately.
questions.check: What restrictions does the ticket state — validity window, refund policy, device lock?
questions.say_example: This ticket is good for <one hour>, can't be refunded, and only works on this device.

questions.question: Does the ticket say ID is required for a reduced fare?
questions.why: The ticket portal explicitly warns that presentation of valid identification will be required when using reduced fare tickets.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the chance to realize they must carry specific physical ID to prove their eligibility, potentially rendering the ticket unusable at the station.
questions.check: Does the ticket portal warn that identification is required when using a reduced fare ticket?
questions.say_example: Reduced fare tickets need ID at the gate. Have that ready.

questions.question: Does the confirmation name landmarks for finding the entrance, not just an address?
questions.why: The confirmation screen provides crucial visual landmarks, like the Tilted Kilt valet and New York Jewelers sign, to help you find the correct entrance.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you miss reading the specific on-the-ground instructions required to successfully locate and park your car.
questions.check: Does the confirmation screen name visual landmarks for finding the entrance?
questions.say_example: Look for the <valet stand> and the <jewelers sign>. Those mark the entrance, not the street address.

questions.question: Does the screen show your updated card balance?
questions.why: The app warns there may be a delay in displaying the latest balance, so refreshing ensures your recent top-up actually went through.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the immediate reassurance of seeing your funds successfully added to the transit card balance.
questions.check: Does the balance shown update after refreshing the screen?
questions.say_example: The balance on screen still hasn't updated after the refresh.

questions.question: Do the account balances shown across these moments agree with each other?
questions.why: The 'My Card' screen initially shows an outdated balance of $2.08, contradicting the $12.08 shown on the earlier 'Top Up Successful' screen before finally updating.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might see the outdated balance before the page refreshes and incorrectly assume the top-up failed, potentially charging your payment method a second time.
questions.check: Does the balance shown on this screen match the balance shown on the earlier top-up confirmation screen?
questions.say_example: The card screen shows <$2.08>, but the top-up screen just showed <$12.08> for the same card.

questions.question: Do you want to download the QR code needed to collect your transit card?
questions.why: The confirmation screen displays a QR code that must be presented at the issuance center to collect the physical card.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to directly save the required QR code to their personal device for later use at the issuance center.
questions.verify_form: The agent either downloaded the collection code or left it on the screen - check whether the file is on the phone; the code has to be shown at a counter and it expires in 48 hours.
questions.check: Does the confirmation screen show a QR code needed to collect the physical transit card, and does it state an expiry window?
questions.say_example: There's a QR code here for collecting the physical card. It expires in <48 hours>, so I'm downloading it now.

questions.question: Should you open the downloaded file to verify the pass?
questions.why: The browser popup shows the image file has finished downloading, prompting a check to ensure the pass is readable and correct.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the immediate visual confirmation that the downloaded pass contains the correct details for your session.
questions.check: Does the downloaded file, once opened, show a readable pass rather than a blank or corrupted image?
questions.say_example: The file downloaded, but opening it shows a blank or broken image, not the pass.

questions.question: Is the menu option about to be picked the one that gets your existing pass, not one that starts a new application?
questions.why: The navigation menu presents multiple similar choices like 'APPLY FOR BUS PASS' and 'DOWNLOAD', so you must identify the specific 'GET e-Pass' button to retrieve your digital ticket.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You miss learning how to navigate the transit portal to retrieve and download your own electronic passes.
questions.check: Does the menu option about to be selected retrieve an existing pass, or does it start a new application instead?
questions.say_example: The menu option I'm about to pick is <Apply for Bus Pass>, which starts a new application, not <Get e-Pass>, which retrieves the one you already have.

questions.question: Which details will you use to retrieve your e-BusPass?
questions.why: The screen offers two distinct lookup methods: entering the specific e-BusPass number or providing a mobile number and date of birth for an OTP verification.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the choice of which personal information to provide and verify when accessing your transit pass.
questions.verify_form: The agent retrieved the pass with either its number or a phone number and a date of birth - check which it used; the second route sends a code to a phone and the first does not.
questions.check: Does the page offer looking up the pass by its number, or by phone number and date of birth with an OTP?
questions.say_example: I can look this up with just the pass number, or with your phone number and birth date instead. The second way sends a code to your phone.

questions.question: Does the app provide an option to add the ticket to your device's digital wallet or save it for offline use?
questions.why: Transit stations often have poor cellular reception, so a digital ticket must be accessible without an internet connection to pass through the gates.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user risks being stranded at the fare gate without internet access if the agent doesn't secure an offline version of the ticket.
questions.verify_form: The agent either saved the ticket for offline use or left it inside the app - check whether it opens with the phone in flight mode; station platforms are where the signal goes.
questions.check: Does the app offer adding the ticket to a digital wallet or saving it for offline use?
questions.say_example: This app can save the ticket for offline use. Stations often lose signal, so I'm saving it now.

questions.question: Did the payment actually process, or did the app loop back to the checkout screen?
questions.why: After the UPI payment step, the app briefly showed a loading dialog but then unexpectedly looped back to the 'Complete Payment' screen without confirming the transaction.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to catch a silent payment failure where the app returns to the checkout screen instead of completing the ticket purchase.
questions.check: After the payment step, does the app show a confirmation, or does it loop back to the checkout screen?
questions.say_example: The payment step showed a loading spinner, then landed back on the same checkout screen instead of a confirmation.

questions.question: Does the page show an order confirmation for the bus pass, or does it end before one shows up?
questions.why: The homepage promised a bus pass delivery in five working days, but the recording ended before an order was placed to confirm this.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the certainty of knowing their transit pass was successfully ordered and will arrive when expected.
questions.check: Does the page show an order confirmation for the bus pass, or does the flow end before one appears despite a stated delivery promise?
questions.say_example: The page promised the bus pass would arrive in <5 working days>, but there's no order confirmation showing the order was actually placed.

questions.question: Does the route on the final ticket match the stops you selected before paying?
questions.why: The final ticket displays a completely different starting and ending stop than the route shown on the payment screen.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses a valid fare for their intended journey because the agent finalized a ticket for the wrong route.
questions.check: Does the route on the final ticket match the stops selected before payment?
questions.say_example: The final ticket shows <Route A>, but you paid for <Route B>.

questions.question: Does the booking time on your final ticket match the time displayed on the payment screen?
questions.why: The final ticket showed a booking time of 13:20:59, which is earlier than the 01:22 PM time displayed before the transaction was initiated.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to notice and dispute a discrepancy where the parking session started earlier than the agreed-upon time.
questions.check: Does the booking time on the final ticket match the time shown on the payment screen just before paying?
questions.say_example: The ticket says it was booked at <13:20>, earlier than the <13:22> shown right before you paid.

questions.question: Does an active parking session or pass actually appear on screen, or does the flow end at the location-permission prompt with no proof of booking?
questions.why: The narrator claims a confirmation will appear, but the video cuts away after a location permission popup without showing the active session or pass.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the certainty that their parking session was successfully booked because the final proof of purchase is missing.
questions.check: Does an active parking session or pass actually appear on screen, or does the flow end at a location-permission prompt or a pending-verification state with no proof of booking?
questions.say_example: The screen stopped at a location-permission prompt. There's no pass or active session showing anywhere after it.

children.label: Use what you bought
children.note: 9.1 where the session can still be lengthened - both meter apps offer it and Kj30 uses it, which sends it back through 5.1, 6.2 and 8.3. 9.2 where the buyer has to go to the place they bought. 9.3 where the artifact has to be scanned before it is worth anything. 9.4 where buying and using are separate acts on separate surfaces. 9.5 where one purchase starts the next. 9.6 where the product is collected off screen entirely.

questions.question: How much additional time do you need to add to your parking session?
questions.why: The screen displays an overlay with adjustable columns for days, hours, and minutes to extend the current parking time.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this decision means the agent might misjudge your schedule, leading to either overpaying for unnecessary time or risking a parking ticket.
questions.verify_form: The agent added time to a session that is already running - check how much; the clock does not restart, so the extension is added to the end time you already had.
questions.check: Does the page ask how much additional time to add, and does it add that to the existing end time rather than restarting the clock?
questions.say_example: How much more time do you need? Whatever I add goes on top of the end time you already had, not from right now.

questions.question: Is the parking extension confirmed with the correct new end time and total cost?
questions.why: Verifying the success message, the new end time of 2:04 PM, and the updated total fee ensures your vehicle is legally parked for the extra time.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the peace of mind of personally confirming the exact time your extended parking session expires.
questions.check: After extending, does the page show a new end time and a new total cost confirming the extension went through?
questions.say_example: The extension screen doesn't show a new end time or a new total, so I can't confirm it actually went through.

questions.question: Does the screen show the fee for the extra time, or just a spinner with no amount?
questions.why: The screen displays an 'Extending your parking session...' spinner but does not show the actual fee being charged for the additional time.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the certainty of knowing exactly how much they were charged for extending their parking time.
questions.check: Does the screen show the fee charged for the extra time (matching or differing from the fee on the original session), or only a processing spinner with no amount?
questions.say_example: The spinner says it's extending, but no fee for the extra time shows here, so there's nothing to compare against the first session's fee.

children.label: Travel to the place you booked

questions.question: Do you want to open directions to the parking location?
questions.why: Tapping the 'Take me there' link launches Apple Maps to provide a route and a 10-minute drive estimate to the destination.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user misses seeing the estimated driving time and having their navigation app automatically routed to the parking spot.
questions.verify_form: The agent opened directions to the garage in a maps app - check that it is the maps app you use and the address it routed to; the pass names an entrance, not just a street.
questions.check: Does the address the directions open to match the location or entrance named on the parking pass?
questions.say_example: The directions are routing to <123 Example Ave>, not the entrance named on your pass.

children.label: Scan the ticket at the gate

questions.question: Is the ticket a code that can be scanned at the gate, rather than something that needs printing?
questions.why: The screen shows a demonstration of a QR code being scanned at a physical metro gate to gain entry.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent cannot physically take the digital ticket and scan it at a real-world transit gate.
questions.check: Does the ticket appear as a scannable code rather than something needing printing?
questions.say_example: Got a scannable ticket code - no printing needed

questions.question: Does the physical card reflect the new balance when you tap it at the gantry?
questions.why: Seeing the green arrow and updated card value on the reader screen confirms that your online purchase successfully synced to the physical card.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the real-world reassurance of seeing the gantry screen display your updated balance as you walk through the gate.
questions.check: Does the card reader show the new balance after tapping, matching the amount just added online?
questions.say_example: The card reader shows the old balance, not the amount you just added online.

questions.question: Should you book a connecting journey from where you arrive?
questions.why: The 'Unreserved E-Ticket' screen allows you to enter a 'To Destination' and proceed to book an onward train.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the choice of whether to purchase your connecting transit fare immediately or wait.
questions.verify_form: The agent either did or did not start a connecting journey from the arrival station - check whether a second ticket is being bought; you may want to buy that leg later, or not at all.
questions.check: Does the page offer booking a connecting journey as a next step from the arrival station?
questions.say_example: There's an option here to book a connecting train onward. That would be a second purchase, not part of this one.
